summary: Iteration 3 — Royal Shades v2 major redesign verified end-to-end. Backend: 28/28 pytest PASS covering role rename (manager->supervisor) + migration check, /api/employees CRUD with RBAC, manual qr_value flow (no auto-gen), buying_price gating (admin-only) across GET /catalogs, GET /catalogs/{id} and POST /scans, PATCH catalog admin-only (403 for supervisor/staff), Excel bulk import template + import-with-errors flow, mobile validation on POST /issues (empty/12abc->400, +971...->200), overdue filter (is_overdue/overdue_days), returns RBAC (staff 403 on GET+POST), dashboard widgets (due_today/due_week/overdue), users admin-only, audit logs carry user_name+record_affected for new actions. Frontend smoke (admin + supervisor): Login page has /rsc-logo.png + 'Royal Shades And Curtains LLC' + 'Dubai · UAE'; dashboard renders all 5 new widgets (Total Issued, Due Today, Due This Week, Overdue, Returned); sidebar shows Employees for admin & supervisor and Users only for admin; Catalogs page shows Bulk Import (admin+supervisor) + Buying column (admin only); Bulk Import dialog has Download Template; Employees page loads; Issues page exposes all 4 filters (Active, Due Today, Due This Week, Overdue). 0 fatal JS errors during the run.

minor.issue: Cookies still set with secure=False (carry-over from iter 2). Low priority hardening.

Range $gte today $lte today+7d would also include overdue items if expected_return_date is in the past AND >= today fails — actual filter is correct, but due_today filter uses $regex on date prefix which works for ISO strings; brittle if non-ISO is stored.

ui_bugs.issue: Brand wordmark 'Royal Shades & Curtains' appears truncated/clipped in the top-left to 'Roya/Shac.. CATA/SUI..' on 1920px viewport — likely a fixed-width container or overflow:hidden issue.

issues: Brand name visually clipped; needs wider container or truncate ellipsis with full text in title attribute.

action_items: Fix sidebar brand truncation so the company name is readable in the top-left.
(Optional, carry-over) Harden auth cookies with secure=True over HTTPS.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1190 lines — getting unwieldy. Recommend splitting into modules (auth.py, catalogs.py, employees.py, reports.py, dashboard.py, scans.py) before next big feature.
Bulk import auto-creates categories/suppliers from row values silently — consider logging this as an audit entry and surfacing in the import report (currently only count of imported/failed is shown).
POST /catalogs/import accepts any file with .xlsx open — validate Content-Type and file size; large XLSX would currently buffer entirely in memory.
issues filter 'due_week' includes today but does not exclude already-overdue items; semantics may differ from UI label.
Mobile validation regex MOBILE_RE allows mixed +-/()/spaces but pure-alpha 'abc' is rejected (good). Consider normalizing on save (strip spaces) for downstream search.

success_rate.frontend: 100% smoke (login branding, dashboard widgets, sidebar RBAC for admin+supervisor, catalogs bulk import dialog, employees CRUD page, issues filters)

test_credentials: Admin: admin@fabriccatalog.com / Admin@123; Supervisor: supervisor1@test.com / Sup@1234 (auto-created); Staff: staff1@test.com / Stf@1234 (auto-created).
seed_data_creation: Tests create TEST_Emp1 employee (then deactivated), RSC-* catalogs, IMP-* catalogs via bulk import, ISS-* and NOQR-* catalogs. All under unique timestamps to avoid collisions on re-runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: v2 backend at 100% (28/28). Two regression suites exist: test_fabric_catalog.py (legacy auth/reports) and test_rsc_v2.py (v2 features). Frontend smoke clean except sidebar brand truncation (low priority). Existing legacy catalog FC-001 still in DB (status=Returned). Bulk import auto-creates referenced category/supplier on the fly.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — all targeted v2 features verified. The only failure during initial run was a too-strict audit-log assertion on legacy entries (pre-v2 records lacked record_affected); the test was relaxed to validate only new actions (catalog_import, employee_created) — the code itself is correct.
